I work mostly as a subcontractor with consulting firms and their client teams, and I take on direct client work too.
Most engagements combine more than one of the areas below.
The common thread is helping capable people do more with their data and their tools.

::: {.dm-grid .dm-grid-2}

::: {.dm-card}
### <i class="bi bi-graph-up" aria-hidden="true"></i> Analytics & modeling

- Energy efficiency program evaluation (EM&V) and savings analysis
- Municipal electrification and energy modeling
- Systems and scenario modeling
- Analysis and reporting in R
:::

::: {.dm-card}
### <i class="bi bi-stars" aria-hidden="true"></i> AI & coding agents for teams

- Find where AI assistants and coding agents fit into your team's work
- Hands-on training with tools like Claude and GitHub Copilot
- Guardrails for data privacy, code review, and acceptable use
- Honest advice on which tools are worth it for your team, and which aren't
:::

::: {.dm-card}
### <i class="bi bi-diagram-3" aria-hidden="true"></i> Data strategy & platforms

- Data model design and review
- Support for client teams through platform migrations
- Reproducible pipelines with Git, Docker, and CI
- Bridging what analysts need with what IT requires
:::

::: {.dm-card}
### <i class="bi bi-lightning-charge" aria-hidden="true"></i> Team efficiency & knowledge

- Internal documentation and knowledge base design
- Curation of shared code, templates, and standards
- Workflow reviews and practical "work hacks"
- Onboarding material that gets new people productive faster
:::

## How engagements work

Most of my work is billed hourly, either as scoped tasks or as a part-time embedded role on your team.
I work remotely and travel when a project calls for it.
The arrangement is the same whether I'm subcontracting for a consulting firm or working directly with your organization.
If your project needs a different arrangement, let's talk about it.
